title: Convinced Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being convinced of the truth of the Gospel before becoming concerned for others. Using John the Baptist as an example, he emphasizes the need to stay with Jesus long enough to be absolutely sure, which then produces a burden for the lost. He contrasts this with the lack of concern in modern churches and calls for a return to holiness.
themes: John the Baptist as a model
the need for personal assurance of salvation
the failure of modern religious systems
holiness and separation from the world
the urgency of the last days

title: An Ensign
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of an 'ensign' as a God-given sign or authority for believers. He contrasts man's failed attempts to save himself through science, education, and human achievement with God's provision of faith and the cross of Christ as the ultimate ensign. Branham encourages the congregation to hold fast to the authority Christ has given His Church.
themes: The cross as the ultimate ensign
Contrast between human achievement and divine provision

title: The Unchangeable God Working In An Unexpectable Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God, who works in unexpected ways, times, and places. Using biblical examples like Moses, Jacob, and the birth of Jesus, he encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises despite opposition or unexpected circumstances.

title: And Thy Seed Shall Possess The Gate Of His Enemy
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise to Abraham that his seed would possess the gate of his enemy, emphasizing that this promise applies to spiritual seed—those who are born of the Spirit. He contrasts true faith in God's Word with reliance on organizations, and stresses the need for testing and separation from the world.

title: The Marriage of the Lamb
summary: William Branham speaks on the marriage of the Lamb, using the analogy of earthly marriage to describe the relationship between Christ and His Church. He emphasizes the need for a genuine connection with Christ through the Holy Spirit, not just an artificial profession of faith.

title: Confirmation Of The Commission
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of divine confirmation for those commissioned by God, using the analogy of a U.S. marshal's credentials. He emphasizes that true believers will have signs following them as promised in Mark 16 and John 14:12, contrasting this with mere human credentials or denominational affiliations.

title: Have Not I Sent Thee?
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for God's people to return to His Word and experience His miracles, using the story of Gideon as an example. He emphasizes that God sends prophets to call His people back, and that true faith is demonstrated by God confirming His Word with signs and wonders.

title: Unbelief Does Not Hinder God
summary: William Branham preaches on Romans 3:3, arguing that unbelief does not hinder God's plans but only destroys the unbeliever. He contrasts faith and unbelief, using biblical examples like Noah and Jesus, and encourages believers to stay rooted in God's Word.
themes: the baptism of the Holy Spirit

title: A Paradox
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of paradox, using biblical examples such as Joshua commanding the sun to stand still, Noah building the ark, Abraham and Isaac, David and Goliath, and Moses leading Israel. He emphasizes that God works in incredible but true ways, and that believers must hold fast to God's Word to see His paradoxical power manifest.

title: Explaining The Ministry
summary: William Branham explains his ministry and the operation of spiritual gifts, emphasizing that God's Word is the ultimate authority and that the same Holy Spirit that worked in biblical times works today. He shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, and calls the congregation to faith in Jesus Christ.

title: Communion
summary: William Branham shares experiences from a recent convention in Arizona, emphasizing the need for genuine communion with God through the Holy Spirit rather than mere ritual. He explains that true communion is a two-way conversation with God, and the bread and wine are only memorials of Christ's sacrifice.

title: Oneness
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of oneness with God, emphasizing that true fellowship requires believing every word of Scripture. He uses Adam and Eve's fall as a warning that doubting even one word breaks union with God, and calls the church to reject man-made creeds and hold fast to God's Word.

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using the example of the Canaanite woman from Matthew 15. He emphasizes that true faith is persistent, rooted in God's Word, and does not mix with unbelief. Branham encourages believers to hold fast to God's promises despite circumstances, as God is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
themes: The Word of God as seed
The Holy Spirit in the Church

title: The Greatest Battle Ever Fought
summary: William Branham announces a forthcoming message on the greatest battle ever fought, drawing from 1 Peter 5:8-10, Ephesians 6:10-17, and Daniel 12:1-14. He explains that the battleground is the human mind, where decisions are made between faith and doubt, and emphasizes the need to clear all channels to let God's Word take root.

title: Expressions
summary: A funeral sermon for Sister Bell, using nature's cycles—trees, flowers, and the sun—as expressions of God's promise of resurrection. Branham comforts the family by affirming that death is not the end but a transition to eternal life, as demonstrated by Christ's resurrection.

title: The End-Time Sign Seed
summary: William Branham preaches on the end-time sign seed, emphasizing that God's Word is the original seed that cannot be hybridized with human creeds or doctrines. He uses examples from nature and Scripture to show that God reveals His secrets to prophets and that believers must accept the Word without doubt to bring forth life.
themes: The Word of God as seed
Faith and acceptance of God's Word

title: Wisdom Versus Faith
summary: William Branham teaches on the two sources of life: wisdom and faith. He traces wisdom back to Satan's deception in the Garden of Eden, where he offered Eve knowledge contrary to God's Word, while faith comes from God and requires believing His Word without reasoning. Branham emphasizes that believers must reject human reasoning and hold fast to God's Word, as faith alone leads to eternal life.
themes: the Word of God as final authority

title: The Signs Of His Coming
summary: William Branham speaks on the signs of Christ's coming, emphasizing that God always gives signs before judgment. He contrasts the dismay of unbelievers with the encouragement believers receive from these signs, and stresses the importance of staying true to God's Word.

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham teaches on the danger of presuming in spiritual matters, using the Old Testament account of Israel at Kadesh-barnea as a warning. He contrasts faith in God's Word with human reasoning and presumption, emphasizing that unbelief is the root of sin. Branham calls believers to stand alone on the Word, fight for every promise, and reject denominational creeds that contradict Scripture.

title: Possessing All Things
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of surviving a rifle accident, then preaches on the believer's inheritance as heirs of all things through Christ, using Abraham's victory over the kings and his meeting with Melchizedek as a type. He encourages believers to claim God's promises by faith and fight the enemy for what is rightfully theirs.

title: The Way of a True Prophet of God
summary: William Branham discusses the characteristics of a true prophet, using the example of Amos from the Bible. He contrasts the prophet's reliance on 'Thus Saith the Lord' with modern religious systems that depend on human credentials and organization. Branham emphasizes that a true prophet is sent by God, fearless in delivering God's Word, and often rejected by the established religious order.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham preaches on the pressures of modern life and the spiritual refuge found in Jesus Christ. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge as a type, he explains that Christ is the place where believers can release their burdens and find safety. He encourages the congregation to cast their cares on God and trust in His promises.
themes: Pressure and tension in modern life
Christ as the city of refuge
The blood of Christ as protection

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the refuge found in God. Using the Old Testament cities of refuge as a type, he explains that Christ is our refuge where we can let off pressure. He encourages believers to trust in God's promises and find safety in His presence.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the true basis of Christian fellowship, emphasizing that it can only be found under the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not through denominations, education, or human efforts. He uses biblical examples like Job and Israel to illustrate that fellowship requires coming under the blood and aligning with God's Word.
themes: The Word of God as the standard
The red heifer as a type of Christ

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, John the Baptist, and the Syrophoenician woman to illustrate how faith in God's Word enables believers to persist despite obstacles. He encourages Christians to remain steadfast in their faith, trusting in God's promises and the evidence of the Holy Spirit.

title: Convinced And Then Concerned
summary: William Branham speaks about the need to be convinced of the truth of the Gospel before becoming concerned for others. He uses biblical examples like John the Baptist, Andrew, Jacob, and Shamgar to illustrate how conviction leads to action, especially in missionary work.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including remarriage after divorce, the resurrection body of the wicked, the meaning of conjunctions in Genesis regarding Eve's conception, and restoration for a backslidden believer. He emphasizes scriptural consistency and the assurance of salvation through Christ.

title: The Conflict Between God and Satan
summary: William Branham preaches on the conflict between God and Satan, emphasizing that God equipped His children with the Word as the ultimate weapon against the enemy. He uses the examples of Eve's fall and the days of Noah to illustrate how human reasoning leads to defeat, while faith in God's Word brings victory.

title: Taking Sides With Jesus
summary: William Branham addresses a gathering of ministers, sharing his heart about the church's position and his own ministry. He discusses the early church model, the need for faithful leadership, and his uncertainty about the future direction of his calling—whether as an evangelist or prophet. He encourages the brethren to remain steadfast and continue building for God's kingdom.
themes: The role of the prophet vs evangelist

title: The End-Time Evangelism
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of end-time evangelism, emphasizing that the last commission of Christ to preach the Gospel with signs following is for all believers. He contrasts the world's nervous anticipation of destruction with the Christian's hope in Christ's appearing, and calls for a return to the pure Word of God without denominational additions.
themes: the appearing and coming of Christ
the Word of God as final authority
moral decay in the last days
the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Perseverance
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using the story of the Syrophoenician woman (Matthew 15:21-28) as a central example. He emphasizes that true faith must be based on God's Word and persist through all barriers—race, criticism, ministerial opposition, and even apparent rejection by Christ. Branham encourages believers to press past the 'sound barrier' of doubt to receive God's promises.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Sufficeth Us
subtitle: 62-0609B
summary: William Branham shares a testimony about leading an infidel to Christ by pointing to the intelligence in nature, such as the sap retreating to the roots of a tree. He emphasizes that God's life is evident all around us, and that true fellowship in Christ is the closest thing to heaven on earth.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
summary: William Branham speaks on the pressures of modern life and the refuge found in Christ. Using biblical examples like the cities of refuge and the Passover, he encourages believers to find safety and peace in the Lord, letting go of worldly anxieties.

title: Presuming
summary: William Branham shares personal testimonies of visions and healings, then teaches from Numbers 14:41-45 on the danger of presuming without God's authority. He warns against taking God's will for granted and emphasizes the need for genuine faith and obedience.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
Behold, A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of Jonah and the wisdom of Solomon, emphasizing that Jesus is greater than both. He encourages believers to look to God's promises rather than symptoms, and warns against rejecting the signs of God's presence in the last days.

title: The Path of Life
summary: William Branham speaks at a Jewish synagogue, expressing his appreciation for the Jewish people and his belief that the Gentile Church will eventually take the message to the Jews. He discusses his ministry, the importance of unity among brethren, and the need for the Holy Spirit in the Church. He emphasizes that true life comes from God and that only those with God's own life (Zoe) can have eternal life.

title: Confirmation And Evidence
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of confirmation and evidence in faith, using biblical examples like Abraham and the Israelites to illustrate how God confirms His promises. He emphasizes that faith is a substance, not just hope, and that the Holy Spirit is the evidence of Christ's resurrection. The sermon includes a prayer line where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment.

title: Letting Off The Pressure
subtitle: 62-0622B
summary: William Branham speaks at Clifton's Cafeteria in Los Angeles, sharing testimonies of healing and encouraging believers to release the pressures of life by finding refuge in Christ, the Rock in a weary land. He uses the analogy of an eagle renewing its strength by beating its head against a rock to illustrate how believers can beat off unbelief and find new life in God.
themes: the Rock in a weary land

title: WHY?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question 'Why?' when God provides a way of escape and people refuse it. He uses the story of Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate how people reject God's remedy and seek worldly alternatives, and calls the church to return to the Holy Ghost and the Word.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of perseverance, using biblical examples such as Noah, Moses, David, Samson, and John the Baptist to illustrate the importance of holding fast to God's Word despite opposition and delay. He emphasizes that true faith requires persistence, being sealed by the Holy Spirit, and waiting on God's timing.
themes: the Ark as type of the Church

title: Super Sign
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of 'super' in the modern world, contrasting human attempts at greatness with God's super sign: the virgin birth of Christ. He emphasizes that Christ is the eternal, supernatural sign, and that believers, as Abraham's spiritual seed, share in His victory over all enemies.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham opens his first meeting in Santa Maria, expressing gratitude for the fellowship and weather. He emphasizes the need to see Jesus as He is revealed in Scripture, noting that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Using the example of Nathanael, he explains that Jesus reveals Himself through prophetic knowledge, and that the same works should be expected today.

title: A Greater Than Solomon Is Here
summary: William Branham preaches on the sign of Jonah and the resurrection, contrasting the faith of Abraham and Jonah with the unbelief of the Pharisees. He emphasizes that the same Messianic signs are present today, and that believers must look to God's promises rather than symptoms.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham encourages believers to trust in Christ's presence and promises, sharing testimonies of healing and divine provision. He emphasizes faith over fear, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate that Christ is with His people in every storm.

title: It Wasn't So From The Beginning
summary: William Branham discusses the nature of visions and spiritual gifts, using biblical examples like Jesus and Lazarus to illustrate how God works through believers. He emphasizes that true ministry comes from yielding to the Holy Spirit, not human intellect, and warns against counterfeit spiritual experiences.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: The Meanest Man In Santa Maria
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings from his early ministry in Arkansas, then preaches on Luke 7:36-50, focusing on the Pharisee's invitation to Jesus and the contrast between the Pharisee's lack of hospitality and the sinful woman's devotion. He emphasizes the need for spiritual preparation and warns against inviting Christ but ignoring Him.

title: To Take On The Whole Armor Of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual armor of God from Ephesians 6, emphasizing that the Word of God is the believer's ultimate weapon against Satan's tactics of reasoning and deception. He contrasts the ever-changing weapons of earthly armies with the unchanging, perfect Word, and warns against intellectualism and false religion that undermine faith.
themes: the Word of God as armor

title: Jehovah-Jireh 2
summary: William Branham continues his series on Abraham, focusing on God's covenant with Abraham and the significance of El Shaddai. He emphasizes the importance of holding fast to God's Word despite circumstances, and contrasts the faith of Abraham with the perversion of the last days. Branham also discusses the restoration of the Bride tree and the need for the Church to return to the pure Word.

title: A Super Sign
summary: William Branham concludes a five-day campaign in Grass Valley, expressing gratitude and love for the congregation. He emphasizes the need for a super sign from God, contrasting human attempts at greatness with God's humble sign of a virgin conceiving Emmanuel. He calls for unity among believers and warns against relying on human achievements.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses faith, divine healing, and the importance of believing God's Word, using Scripture to show that Jesus' works testify of His identity.

title: From That Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of recognizing God's moving in the present, using the example of Israel following the Pillar of Fire. He discusses the need for the Church to remain open to the Holy Spirit beyond denominational boundaries, and emphasizes that true Pentecost is an experience, not an organization. He also shares personal testimonies and reflections on the assurance of resurrection and the authority believers have in Christ.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of uncertainty in the world, using 1 Corinthians 14:8 as a text. He shares personal testimonies of divine guidance and healing, emphasizing that anything uncertain cannot be trusted and that believers must be certain in their faith and actions.

title: Life
summary: William Branham shares personal anecdotes and reflections on unity among Christians, the dangers of rigid organization, and the importance of fellowship. He emphasizes that God is a God of variety and that believers should work together despite differences. The sermon concludes with a meditation on eternal life through Christ.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being perseverant in faith, using biblical examples like the Canaanite woman, Noah, Moses, David, and Samson. He emphasizes that true perseverance comes from hearing God's Word and holding onto His promises despite opposition or delay.

title: A Testimony On The Sea
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of character and faith, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water to illustrate that believers must trust in the resurrected Christ. He emphasizes that outward expressions of faith must align with the Word of God, and that the Holy Spirit seeks character in the Bride of Christ.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Suffice Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire of the human heart to see God, using the text John 14:8 where Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. Branham illustrates God's presence in nature through personal anecdotes and calls believers to trust in the Holy Ghost as instinctively as animals trust their God-given instincts.

title: A Testimony Upon The Sea
summary: William Branham preaches on the testimony of the disciples after Jesus fed the five thousand, using the account of Peter walking on water as a metaphor for faith. He encourages believers to trust in God's Word and maintain their healing despite temporary setbacks.

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the desire to see Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to look beyond outward appearances and seek the anointed Christ, who is the Word made flesh. Branham stresses the importance of faith in God's Word and the simplicity of the Gospel.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: God Has A Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provided way for humanity to escape judgment and find salvation. Using examples from nature and Scripture, he emphasizes that God always provides a way, and man must walk in it by faith and obedience to His Word.

title: Perseverant
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of perseverance in faith, using the story of the Canaanite woman and Abraham as examples. He emphasizes that true faith is a substance that holds onto God's promises despite circumstances, and encourages believers to be persistent in their trust in God's Word.

title: In His Presence
summary: William Branham preaches on the profound effect of coming into the presence of God, using biblical examples like Isaiah, Moses, and Paul to show how holy men recognized their sinfulness. He emphasizes that encountering God transforms a person, leading to confession, cleansing, and a responsibility to share the message with others.

title: The Key To The Door
summary: William Branham preaches on the key of faith that unlocks the door to God's promises, using Revelation 20:1 as a text. He emphasizes that Jesus is the Door and faith is the key, illustrating with biblical heroes and personal testimonies. The sermon includes announcements about church building, a baby dedication, and upcoming meetings.
themes: Faith as the key to unlock God's promises
Jesus Christ as the only Door to salvation, healing, and peace
The importance of holding to God's Word over creeds and denominations
Personal testimony of God's faithfulness in calling and provision
The danger of unbelief and the need for full Gospel faith

title: The Influence Of Another
summary: William Branham preaches on the influence of King Uzziah on the prophet Isaiah, emphasizing the importance of staying in one's God-given calling and not being lifted up with pride. He warns against compromising the Word for organizational creeds and urges believers to remain faithful to God's order.
themes: The power of a godly example

title: The Stature of a Perfect Man
summary: William Branham teaches on building the living Tabernacle of God, emphasizing that believers must be born again and then add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, and love to their faith. He explains that these qualities cannot be manufactured but naturally flow from a changed nature in Christ.

title: A Guide
summary: William Branham preaches on the Holy Spirit as the God-given Guide for believers, using the analogy of a wilderness guide to illustrate the necessity of following the Spirit's leading into all truth. He warns against relying on human creeds, denominations, or traditions, and emphasizes that the Holy Spirit will always align with the Word of God.

title: Ordination
subtitle: 62-1104E
summary: William Branham discusses the biblical basis for ordination, emphasizing that gifts and callings come from God alone, not through human impartation. He then ordains Brother McKinney, a former Methodist minister, by laying on of hands and the right hand of fellowship. The sermon concludes with a communion service and feetwashing.

title: Dedication
subtitle: 62-1111M
summary: William Branham speaks at a rededication service for a small church in Elizabethtown, Kentucky. He uses the biblical examples of David's desire to build a temple and Solomon's construction to illustrate that God's true temple is not a building but the hearts of believers. He emphasizes the need for personal dedication and the filling of the Holy Spirit.

title: Why I'm Against Organized Religion
summary: William Branham explains his opposition to organized religion, arguing that it is unscriptural and based on human tradition rather than God's Word. He uses biblical examples such as Adam, Nimrod, Korah, and the Pharisees to show that organization leads to rejection of God's messengers and message. Branham emphasizes that salvation is a birth, not a membership, and calls believers to separate from man-made systems.

title: Return And Jubilee
summary: William Branham speaks on the biblical concept of Jubilee from Leviticus 25, drawing parallels to the Pentecostal outpouring fifty years prior in Louisiana. He warns against losing the original spiritual inheritance through organization and creeds, calling believers to return to the Holy Spirit and the Word.

title: The Way Back
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to return to God through the inoculation of the Blood of Jesus Christ and the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He uses the story of King Ahaziah and Elijah to illustrate how people often reject God's provided way back, preferring popular but ineffective methods. Branham calls for a genuine new birth that involves dying to self and taking God's serum for sin.

title: All Things
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'All Things' from Romans 8:32, emphasizing that all things are ours through Christ. He discusses the importance of sincerity in worship, warning against ritualistic forms that lack power, and stresses that only the shed blood of Jesus Christ can bridge the chasm between man and God.

title: Convinced And Then Concerned
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to be convinced of God's Word and then concerned for others. He contrasts the early church's zeal with modern complacency, emphasizing that true conviction leads to action and concern for the lost.

title: The Countdown
summary: William Branham uses the analogy of a countdown for a space launch to describe the progression of the church through the seven church ages, culminating in the rapture. He contrasts the natural astronaut age with the spiritual astronaut age, urging believers to rise above earthly denominations and creeds to be ready for Christ's return.

title: Remembering The Lord
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of remembering Christ, especially through communion, and warns against the dangers of prejudice, jealousy, and personal gain that can cause one to miss their visitation. He uses examples from Scripture, such as Herod and Judas, to illustrate the consequences of failing to recognize and honor the Lord.

title: The Falling Apart of the World
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message at the tabernacle, discussing the true meaning of Christmas and critiquing its commercial and pagan origins. He emphasizes the importance of spiritual birth over church membership and dedicates several children to the Lord.

title: The Reproach For The Cause Of The Word
summary: William Branham shares a vision of five mighty angels and reflects on the reproach that God's servants bear for the sake of His Word. He encourages believers to stand firm in faith despite scoffers and trials, using examples from Noah and personal testimonies of healing.

title: Absolute
summary: William Branham shares a personal testimony about the resolution of a tax case with the U.S. government, emphasizing the importance of having an 'absolute'—a firm, Christ-centered foundation. He draws on biblical examples like Job, Abraham, Moses, and Paul to illustrate how unwavering faith in God's Word enables believers to stand firm amidst trials.

title: The Contest
summary: In this New Year's Eve sermon, William Branham encourages believers to recognize the spiritual contest between the Church and Satan, emphasizing the power of God's Word as the believer's strength. He shares a testimony of a healing in India to demonstrate God's power over demonic forces, and calls the congregation to enter the new year with faith and the full armor of God.
